### Insights and directions

The starting idea yields three insights. First, a zero-initialized residual preserves SASRec’s initial predictions, enabling a controlled architectural extension. Second, a causal five-item window explicitly represents recent evidence, addressing the reported persistence of older interests. Third, a single global coefficient cannot distinguish a coherent recent sequence from unrelated purchases; recency alone does not establish current intent.

The supplied literature suggests three complementary insights. CoDeR+ motivates distinguishing sustained demand shifts from fluctuations, although its applicability here remains untested. Scarcelli et al. motivate sequence-aware perturbations; the supplied Pandey et al. summary cautions that masking sensitivity can reflect unfamiliar inputs. Subbiah et al. motivate separating sampled-ranking behavior from catalog behavior: training margins cannot substitute for pinned validation HR@10.

These insights organize three directions: adaptive recent-history representations, controlled attribution diagnostics, and evidence-grounded recommendation judgments. Titles, descriptions, and timestamps can support interpretation; they cannot establish unobserved compatibility or satisfied needs.

### Framework

| Layer | Existing approach | Proposed extension | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Representation | SASRec plus global recent residual | Coherence-gated recent residual | Embedding coherence may reflect broad associations |
| Diagnosis | Embedding geometry and sampled margins | Matched residual ablation and history perturbations | Sensitivity does not identify causal intent |
| Selection | Four-category macro validation HR@10 | Preserve pinned evaluation | Adaptive search can overfit validation |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty, each out of 10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Coherence-gated recent residual** | **5/7/3** | Originality: modest adaptive extension; potential: tests coherent recency; difficulty: small implementation | Originality: familiar gating; potential: noisy geometry; difficulty: causal masking needs care |
| Learned two-window residual mixture | 4/6/4 | Originality: simple timescale combination; potential: adapts persistence; difficulty: reuses embeddings | Originality: established pattern; potential: more selection variance; difficulty: additional gates and ablations |
| Perturbation-guided residual regularization | 6/7/6 | Originality: connects attribution and training; potential: explicit dependence control; difficulty: standard tensor operations | Originality: related consistency objectives; potential: may enforce incorrect invariances; difficulty: extra forward passes |

### Selected idea

At 10% progress, prioritize **coherence-gated recent residuals**, a small, falsifiable extension of the starting idea. For each position, compute coherence from the last five nonpadding item embeddings available at that position. Use it to attenuate the recent residual when recent items disagree. Coherence is an observable model statistic, not a user trait or verified intent label.

```text
h = SASRec(sequence)
for position t:
    E = embeddings(last five nonpadding items through t)
    r = mean(E)
    c = mean pairwise cosine(E), or 0 if fewer than two items
    g = clamp((1 + c) / 2, 0, 1)
    z[t] = h[t] + alpha * g * r
# alpha starts at zero; score with existing item embeddings
```

Preserve routing, splits, seeds, and training defaults. Share this representation across training, predictor generation, and diagnostic scoring. Compare against SASRec and the original scalar residual using pinned macro validation HR@10; report branch ablation separately. No improvement is established by the supplied evidence.

idea.description: Add a zero-initialized scalar residual whose causal five-item mean is gated by pairwise embedding coherence.
idea.motivation: Recent coherent interests may provide stronger evidence than isolated historical associations. A coherence gate offers a minimal way to test that hypothesis without inventing user traits or unavailable product attributes.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four dataset routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Compute each window using only nonpadding items through the current position; mask padding outputs. Compute cosine similarities with a numerical epsilon and exclude self-pairs. Initialize the directly learned scalar alpha to zero. Update the predictor writer to serialize and reconstruct the same architecture. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Have log2feats and predict_score use the actual trained representation. Report gate distributions and scaled residual norms alongside existing margins; these are diagnostics, not validation metrics. Preserve empty or unavailable metadata fields without fabrication. Bound comparisons within the remaining shared GPU budget.
idea.pseudocode:
H = causal_sasrec(sequence)
for each batch row and position t:
    ids = last_nonpadding(sequence[:t+1], count=5)
    E = item_emb(ids)
    if len(ids) == 0: continue
    R = mean(E)
    C = mean_off_diagonal_cosine(E) if len(ids) >= 2 else 0
    G = clamp((1 + C) / 2, 0, 1)
    H[t] = H[t] + alpha * G * R
return H

originality.positive: Introduces an explicit coherence condition into the supplied global recent-residual proposal.
originality.negative: Gating, local pooling, and residual connections are established techniques; novelty is limited to the specific combination.

future_potential.positive: Provides a compact hypothesis that can support later work on adapting recency to observed history structure.
future_potential.negative: Embedding coherence can encode broad topical similarity and may suppress useful transitions between complementary items.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires only a short causal pooling branch and one learned scalar.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct padding treatment, per-position windows, and agreement between training, generated inference, and diagnostic decomposition require careful implementation.

related_work.title: CoDeR+ (2026; supplied search result)
contributions: The supplied summary distinguishes demand shifts from noisy fluctuations, motivating adaptive treatment of recent histories.
limitations: Does not establish that embedding coherence identifies current intent in these four datasets.

related_work.title: Scarcelli et al. (2025; supplied search result)
contributions: The supplied summary describes minimal sequence edits that change recommendations, motivating sequence-aware diagnostic interventions.
limitations: Recommendation sensitivity does not establish causal user intent or benchmark improvement.

related_work.title: Pandey et al. (2026 preprint; supplied search result)
contributions: The supplied summary motivates masking-robust temporal attribution and cautions against interpreting raw attention as faithful attribution.
limitations: Deletion effects may reflect unfamiliar inputs; this proposal does not implement its separately trained attribution probe.

related_work.title: Subbiah et al. (2024; supplied search result)
contributions: The supplied summary discusses negative-sampling rank corrections for ranking objectives.
limitations: Does not validate larger training margins as evidence of improved full-catalog recommendations or validate the proposed gate.
